# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 21 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 21 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_021_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 13

**1** "Those from the sixth mountain with its clefts large and small — who are they?" "Those with the small clefts are those who have grievances against one another and are somewhat at odds. Many of them grow weary through their disputes, but repentance is available to them, and those who repent will live to God. Those with the large clefts are those who quarrel constantly and hold lasting ill will toward each other. **2** These have been cast from the tower and rejected. Repentance is hard to come by for them, but if they do repent they will have a place in the building; if they refuse, they will perish." **3** "Those from the seventh mountain — the cheerful and flourishing one — these are those who were submissive and gentle and free from quarreling. They always rejoiced in the servants of God, clothed themselves in the Holy Spirit, and always showed mercy to all. They gave freely to everyone from their own resources, without reproach or hesitation." **4** "The Lord therefore sees their simplicity and undivided goodness and fills them with the blessings of his good things. They are worthy of eternal life because of their good character, their innocence, and their labor for the Lord's servants." **5** "Those from the eighth mountain — with its springs where all creatures came to drink — these are the apostles and teachers who proclaimed to the whole world, teaching the word of the Lord in holiness and truth, holding back from all evil desires and walking always in righteousness and truth. **6** Because of this they are always at peace with one another and are established in peace, and they will live to God." **7** "Those from the ninth mountain — the wilderness with its serpents and deadly beasts — these are the deacons who administered badly; they stole from the substance of widows and orphans and profited personally from their service. If they persist in this conduct they will die and have no hope of life; but if they repent and complete their ministry in purity, life remains possible for them." **8** "Those from the tenth mountain — the shaded one where flocks rested — these are the bishops and those given to hospitality who always welcomed God's servants into their homes with joy and sincerity. These bishops sheltered the afflicted and the widows in their care without ceasing, and they conducted themselves with holiness in everything." **9** "All of these will be under the Lord's shelter forever. Those who did these things are glorious before God, and their place is already set among the angels — if they continue to keep the Lord's commandments." **10** "Those from the eleventh mountain — laden with fruit — these are those who suffered for the name of the Lord and surrendered their lives and possessions readily and wholeheartedly, suffering willingly for his name." **11** "Those from the twelfth mountain — the entirely white one — these are the innocent ones, the infants in faith, into whose hearts no evil ever entered; they did not know what wickedness was, and they remained in childlike innocence always." **12** "These will rest forever and without doubt live with God. Blessed are all of you who have cast off wickedness and clothed yourselves with innocence — you will be among the first to live to God."

---

*LOGOS note: The twelfth mountain culminates the sequence: innocent infants in faith who never knew evil. The final beatitude extends the blessing to anyone who returns to such innocence — making the entire twelve-mountain catalog a call to repentance and renewal.*
